# gui-templates

Everything the GUI Builder's "Build in Studio" mode uses.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `_kit.lua` | LurongUI Kit: the Luau library that draws studded panels, outlined text, buttons, bars, tabs, the wheel... It is prepended to every script that runs in Studio. |
| `GEMINI_GUI_AGENT.md` | The instruction prompt Gemini gets (workflow, Kit reference, layout and design rules). The template catalog is appended to it automatically. |
| `<id>.lua` | One template each. Gemini uses these as the Lua code source for what it builds. |

## Adding a template

Drop a `.lua` file in this folder. It is picked up on the next request (no restart) when running from source; for a packaged build run `node scripts/build-gui-templates.cjs` or the normal secure build, which packs this folder into `gui-templates.bundle.cjs`.

A template is a complete build script that only needs `Kit`:

```lua
--[[ LURONG GUI TEMPLATE
id: pet_inventory
name: Pet Inventory
style: studded
tags: pets, inventory, equip, grid
description: One or two sentences Gemini reads to decide when to use it.
customize: what is meant to be changed (title, items table, colours...)
]]

local screen = Kit.screen("PetInventoryGui")
local win = Kit.window(screen, { name = "Pets", title = "Pets", theme = "blue", size = { 1000, 760 } })
-- build inside win.content ...
Kit.controller(screen)
return Kit.report(screen)
```

- `id` must be unique; `tags` are what the app matches against the user's request.
- Keep the data (items, prices, days) in a table at the top so it is obvious what to replace.
- Sizes are design pixels on a 1920 x 1080 canvas.
- Test it with the template picker's **Insert as-is** button in the GUI Builder: it builds the file in the open Studio place without calling Gemini.
